`abstract class BackTweenEquation`<br/>
**Extends:** [`TweenEquation`](/reference/animation/tweenequation/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.animation.tween.equation` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [BackTweenEquation.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/animation/tween/equation/BackTweenEquation.java)

Easing curves that move back a little before they start or go past the end before they settle.

![The Back easing curves in a dark grey frame that marks 0 and 1: IN in blue, OUT in light grey, IN_OUT in grey, named under the curves, with one dot per curve that runs along it from the start to the end](/captures/catalog-easing-backtweenequation.webp)

## Description

Each constant is also in [`TweenEquations`](/reference/animation/tweenequations/), as `BACK_IN`, `BACK_OUT` and `BACK_IN_OUT`.
`overshoot(...)` gives the same curve with a larger or smaller swing, whose `toString()` carries it: `"Back.OUT(2.5)"`, which [`TweenEquations.of`](/reference/animation/tweenequations/#TweenEquations-method-of) reads back.

## Property details

<a id="BackTweenEquation-property-overshoot"></a>

### overshoot

- `this overshoot(float overshoot)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>
- `float getOvershoot()` 

**Default:** 

How far the curve swings past its ends: `0F` gives no swing, larger values swing further.
`overshoot(float)` returns a curve of the same direction with that swing and leaves this one unchanged.

## Constant and field details

<a id="BackTweenEquation-constant-IN"></a>

### IN

`BackTweenEquation IN` 

Moves back a little before it starts.

<a id="BackTweenEquation-constant-OUT"></a>

### OUT

`BackTweenEquation OUT` 

Goes past the end a little before it settles.

<a id="BackTweenEquation-constant-IN_OUT"></a>

### IN_OUT

`BackTweenEquation IN_OUT` 

Moves back a little at the start and goes past the end a little.

<a id="BackTweenEquation-field-overshoot"></a>

### overshoot

`float overshoot` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

How far the curve swings past its ends: `0F` gives no swing, larger values swing further.
`overshoot(float)` returns a curve of the same direction with that swing and leaves this one unchanged.
